features.text: The patient is 82 years old and male.
The patient experienced an acute on chronic heart failure exacerbation requiring hospitalization.
The patient had shortness of breath and swelling in the ankles.
The patient had to call 911 due to shortness of breath.
The swelling in the ankles has been ongoing for a while but worsened before hospitalization.
The shortness of breath came on suddenly, with no prior symptoms.
The patient currently feels much better and has no trouble breathing or swelling.
The patient has chronic kidney disease and hypertension.
This was the patient's first acute heart failure episode.
The patient was given a diuretic (Bumex) during hospitalization.
The patient is currently taking Bumex, 2 milligrams once a day.
The patient is currently taking Cozaar and Norvasc for blood pressure.
The patient's echocardiogram showed a preserved ejection fraction of 55%, abnormal diastolic filling, and mild to moderate mitral regurgitation.
A renal artery ultrasound was ordered to check for secondary causes of kidney disease.
The patient has stage three chronic kidney disease.
The patient does not have the exact numbers for serum creatinine, eGFR, or electrolytes at the moment.
The patient is awaiting further blood work to ensure they can handle their medications.
